Key patterns:
- **Policy accretion** (largest): domain files restating platform standards (Forma, Folio, API, isolation, Strata) and "Support X" umbrellas (UNB-ACC-009, -010, UNB-NAV-014) that have no testable content.
- **Conservative interpretation / human compensating for technology**: review of every NAV (UNB-NAV-008), nine valuation states (UNB-NAV-005), advisor re-consent for sponsor funding choices (UNB-GFUND-012), per-journal approval (UNB-ACC-022). Decided records (RCD-035, RCD-020, RCD-017) already allow exception-driven control.
- **Digitized paper**: close checklists (UNB-ACC-017), recurring journals (UNB-ACC-034), separately prepared audit schedules (UNB-ACC-020).
- **Department silos / legacy systems**: operating ERP functions (AP, AR, budgeting, payroll, consolidation) and wealth-management conventions (fund-level TWR/MWR, native rebalancing).
- **Fee-model dependency**: FeeBase segmentation and daily accrual (RR-UNB-NAV-033-r1, UNB-XIN-ERP-001) follow from basis-point pricing (SPF-FIN-008). These are correct given the model; they are listed so the economics group can price the alternative.
- **Information unavailable**: per-grant liquidation planning (UNB-GFUND-011) arises only because no pool cash buffer was assumed.

**Scope.** 370 requirements (310 baseline, 30 discovery-new UNB-XIN, 20 reconciliation-new UNB-RCN, 10 RR refinement records) covering grants, grant events/exceptions, charity registry/knowledge/external data/rules, payments/banking, nonprofit grantmaking and regulatory status. One register row per id (count verified = 370, executed validation script). Method: each row read against its source text, the reconciliation/discovery decisions (reports 16, 17, 18) and cost evidence; numbers are derived by stated arithmetic. Same-model analysis: not independent validation.

**Normalisation inputs.** 10,000 accounts x 8 grants per account-year [S unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/15-economics/economic-model.md:29, expected case] = **80,000 grants** [D]. Labour rate $55.45/h [S unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/15-economics/economic-model.md:96, the model's own unreconciled rate, GAP-040].

**Dollars [D at $55.45/h, S unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/15-economics/economic-model.md:96].** Literal: 10,667 h = **$591k** per 10k accounts ($59 per account; $7.39 per grant). Target: 766 h = **$42.5k** ($4.25 per account; $0.53 per grant). Reduction ~93% [D]. With the manual-revalidation counterfactual the literal figure would be ~19,000 h.

**Comparison with industry evidence.** Industry process pools: routine eligibility verification ~$139k per 1M grants ($0.14/grant), marked "should not exist per grant" [S daf-landscape:research/mission-2026-11-14/ai-economics-replacement-analysis.md:56]; non-standard diligence ~$1.25M per 1M grants [S daf-landscape:research/mission-2026-11-14/ai-economics-replacement-analysis.md:57; unbound:requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/industry/grt.md:206-207]. Scaled to 80,000 grants: ~$11k + ~$100k = **~$111k** per 10k accounts [D]. So (a) the literal reading (~$591k) is ~5x the observed-pool equivalent: requirements as written would build a heavier vetting operation than the industry runs; (b) routine verification is already cheap, and grt.md concludes "automating routine verification further adds little" [S unbound:requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/industry/grt.md:224]; (c) the remaining money is in non-standard diligence and external practitioner fees (~$4k typical international ED, $50k minimum at RCF [S unbound:requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/industry/grt.md:208]), which reuse (ED valid ~2 years [S unbound:requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/industry/grt.md:209]) and intermediaries (UNB-XIN-NPG-002) address - not AI. AI's best fit is evidence assembly on the non-standard residual, after redesign [S daf-landscape:research/mission-2026-11-14/ai-economics-replacement-analysis.md:127]. Our target residual excludes external ED/ER fees and R1 excludes direct foreign/ER grants (RCD-014; report 17), so the target is not comparable to the full P07 pool.

**Irreducible human review [observation + inference].** (1) Non-standard recipient classes: ERRequired, CounselReview, foreign without ED (counsel; R1 rejects them). (2) True or unresolved sanctions potential matches and blocked-property decisions (OFAC strict liability; SCV-04). (3) Release of related-party payee holds (independent compliance on counsel determination, UNB-RCN-GRT-002). (4) Ambiguous identity, impersonation and suspected fraud. (5) Charity disputes. (6) Discretionary holds under board policy (UNB-XIN-NPG-006). (7) Successor/payee substitution approval (UNB-XIN-NPG-005). (8) Post-distribution violation determinations and liability (counsel/CPA, UNB-XIN-NPG-008). (9) Rule, FreshnessPolicy, MaterialityTable and override changes under dual control. (10) Independent after-the-fact sampling of automatic decisions (UNB-XIN-CLM-005). Total ~766 h per 10k accounts [D], dominated by (1)-(4).

**Guardrails so elimination does not weaken controls.** Release-time status and sanctions checks are never skipped (SPR-GRT-001); outage = hold, not eligible (UNB-RULE-009); AI never clears holds (SPR-GRT-002); metrics: straight-through rate, manual touches per 1,000 grants, evidence reuse ratio, false-hold and false-clear rates, time to detect material events (CA-180 item 10; UNB-GEX-023; UNB-XIN-ECO-007).

section: Scope, method and evidence status (ORG group)
markdown:
**Phases owned:** Two (enterprise work inventory), Three (minimum-touch organization, human-intervention taxonomy, assignment models, charity-vetting operating design), Six (organizational structure and staffing). DOM code **ORG**.

**Method.** 143 activities (SPW-001..SPW-143) were enumerated across 31 business functions from the requirement corpus (each activity cites existing requirement IDs; evidence column gives `unbound:<path>:<line>` from `requirements/reconciliation/2026-11-23/data/inventory.csv` or the gap/refinement JSONL). For each activity two human-minute figures are recorded per driver unit: *conventional* and *minimum-touch*. **All minutes and volumes are assumptions [A]**; no operational measurement exists (economic-model.md:3). Volumes at 100k accounts reuse the baseline's grants (8/account) and contributions (2/account) (daf-landscape:research/ai-native-daf-enterprise/09-financial-models/financial-and-staffing-models.md:18-21 @6b3083a, where they are themselves partly [A]). Aggregates were **executed** by a Python script over the JSONL (output reported below); they are **[D]** (derived arithmetic from [A] inputs), not measurements.

**Independence caveat.** All perspectives here come from one model in one session. Agreement between this analysis and earlier same-model passes (theoretical-validation, discovery) is **not** independent validation.

**Output files:** work-inventory.jsonl (143), roles.jsonl (24), findings.jsonl (13), requirements.jsonl (2), refinements.jsonl (3), scenarios.jsonl (7), decisions.jsonl (6), rejected.jsonl (7).

**What was inventoried.** 143 recurring or event-driven activities in 31 functions, each with trigger, purpose, decision, beneficiary, consequence of omission, elimination/prevention/consolidation options, automation class, human-required conditions, frequency driver, minutes, existing requirement IDs, duplication and dependencies.

**Automation class (minimum-touch target):** deterministic 57, mixed 63, human 19, ai-assisted 4. AI-assisted is deliberately rare: AI is used where evidence is unstructured (answers grounded in an approved corpus, regulatory-change reading); everything rule-expressible is deterministic first (mission principle; organization §3, unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/03-organization/organization-and-authority.md:48-60).

**Executed aggregate (Python over work-inventory.jsonl) — direct activity time only:**

Direct time excludes supervision, training, utilisation loss and engineering. The conventional derived figure at 100k (237.0 direct FTE) is well below the Vanguard-ratio comparator of 431 employees at 100k [S, daf-landscape:research/ai-native-daf-enterprise/09-financial-models/financial-and-staffing-models.md:25,37 @6b3083a], so the inventory **undercounts conventional work** (no management layers, rework, sales, IT build). It is used only to compare the two columns on identical scope, not to claim a conventional headcount.

**Reading the numbers.**
- Five functions carry most minimum-touch hours: grant approval/distribution (exception decisions SPW-060), complex assets (SPW-026, SPW-030), charity vetting (ED/ER SPW-053/054), payment exceptions, and service. All five are **exception-driven**; their human minutes scale with volume × exception share.
- Functions that are almost entirely eliminated as human work: grant recommendations, contributions, investments, accounting postings, statements, acknowledgments — deterministic once inputs are authoritative.
- 3 activities exist **only** in the minimum-touch model (SPW-088, SPW-116, SPW-125): independent sampling of straight-through decisions, AI configuration and model-risk review, cost initiatives. They add ≈720 h/yr regardless of scale [D] (SPF-ORG-009). Omitting them would overstate savings.
- Moving work to donors, charities or vendors is not counted as elimination: self-service items (e.g. SPW-007, SPW-014) keep a residual minute figure, and outsourced work (liquidation agents, CPA, counsel) is costed as purchased services in the staffing model.

**Elimination vs prevention vs automation.** `can_eliminate` = Y for 15 activities (timers, generated registers, automatic remittance, flag expiry), partial for 65, N for 63 (legally required, independent control or reserved judgment — these are simplified or automated, not removed).

**Critical paths (activity level; a delay or failure anywhere stops the outcome):**

| Outcome | Path | Human-required nodes in minimum-touch | Single points of failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routine grant paid | SPW-043 → SPW-047 → SPW-049/050 → SPW-059 → SPW-062 → SPW-066 → SPW-068 → SPW-081 → SPW-075 → SPW-077 → SPW-013 | none when all gates pass; SPW-077 certification monthly | charity status source freshness (SPW-050/051); payment gate; bank file ingestion (SPW-081) |
| Exception grant paid | … SPW-059 → SPW-060 (A4) → [SPW-053/054 if foreign/ER] → SPW-068 … | SPW-060, SPW-053/054 | eligible decider availability (UNB-SMP-ORG-002); December surge |
| Contribution credited and acknowledged | SPW-019/021 → SPW-022 → SPW-075 → SPW-081/083 → SPW-077 | none for routine | processor/bank files; acknowledgment template gate |
| Complex gift to grantable value | SPW-002 → SPW-026 → SPW-029 → SPW-030 → SPW-021 → SPW-022/027/028 | SPW-026, SPW-029 (acceptance authority) | gift-acceptance authority capacity |
| Payee change to safe payment | SPW-067 → SPW-066 (cooling-off) → SPW-068 → SPW-070 on return | SPW-067 when risk signals | payee approver ≠ releaser |
| Period close | SPW-040, SPW-081, SPW-082, SPW-083 → SPW-075 → SPW-077 → SPW-013 → SPW-084 → SPW-095 | SPW-077 certification, SPW-082 unexplained breaks | independent reconciler (TVR-ORG-003) |
| Sponsor launch | SPW-140 → SPW-106 → SPW-108 → SPW-105 → SPW-121 (board) | all (one-time) | board delegation resolution (UNB-RCN-WF-016) |

**Structural observations.** (1) Charity vetting and payments are upstream of grant approval; their freshness, not human review, gates throughput. (2) Reconciliation feeds accounting and tax; it is the main enterprise-level control path and must sit outside the payment chain. (3) Governance → sponsor administration → every decision is the authority spine: a lapsed delegation suspends routine approval platform-wide (UNB-RCN-WF-016), so DoA maintenance (SPW-108) is on every critical path even though it is rare.

**Net effect.** Most duplication is **across organizations** (sponsors, custodians, banks, partners) rather than inside one sponsor. Inside one sponsor, a one-system design (REQ-X-057) removes most departmental duplication. Across organizations, only **factual evidence** can be shared; **decisions and legal reliance** remain per sponsor. That limit caps the savings from a shared registry at the factual-verification portion of vetting (see charity vetting operating design).

Four models per function. *Conventional* = departmental, human review of most items. *Improved conventional* = same organization with better tools. *AI-native* = the baseline design (deterministic routine + AI flags + human exceptions). *Minimum-touch* = the smallest human footprint that keeps every legal, fiduciary and independent-control duty, with elimination and prevention applied before automation. Percentages marked [D] come from the executed inventory aggregate at 100k accounts; [A] are judgments.

**Cross-cutting rules for the minimum-touch model.**
1. A human touch exists only when it falls in one of the human-intervention classes (next section) and the creating rule says so (UNB-SMP-ORG-001).
2. Deterministic before AI; AI output is evidence, never authority (REQ-X-017; RR-AIN-003-r1).
3. Automation failure fails safe to hold or to an eligible human — never fail-open (REQ-X-017 acceptance).
4. Every exception class has a prevention owner; recurring exceptions become REQ-X-042 proposals.
5. The minimum-touch model adds an independent sampling control (UNB-XIN-CLM-005) because fewer humans see routine decisions; its cost is counted.

| Function group | Recommendation | Condition / dependency |
|---|---|---|
| Onboarding, account administration, contributions, grant recommendations, investments, custody, accounting, statements | Minimum-touch now | Authoritative inputs; templates counsel-approved |
| Grant approval | Minimum-touch for routine grants | OD-01/TVC-003: counsel confirms board-delegated deterministic approval preserves exclusive legal control |
| Charity vetting | Minimum-touch with reason-coded exceptions | RR-REQ-X-007-r3; counsel on cross-sponsor reliance |
| Payments | Minimum-touch routine release; human exceptions | SPD-ORG-001 on SoD treatment of the gate; ACH-first |
| Complex assets, ED/ER, succession, fraud investigations, reconsideration, complaints | Improved conventional with specialist pools | These are legally or fiduciarily human; reduce volume by routing (intermediaries, pre-verified successors), not by automation |
| Service | Minimum-touch with guaranteed human option | Accessibility and complaint handling stay human |
| Governance, executive, BCP, sponsor admin | Minimum-touch inputs (generated packs, computed coverage); human decisions | Configuration minimised |
| IA, tax prep, counsel, HR, reconciliation review (small scale) | Purchase | Independence and competence; SPD-ORG-006 |
| BD, marketing, relationship management | Commercial choice; not part of the control floor | — |

**Rule zero: AI involvement alone never triggers human review.** A human touch is justified only by one of the nine classes below, evaluated on the *decision and evidence*, not on which component produced the evidence. A rule that would route "because AI was used" or "because AI confidence < x" must instead cite the evidentiary condition (normally Ambiguous evidence or Novel circumstances) — enforced at rule publication by UNB-SMP-ORG-001.

**Classification order.** Evaluate 1 → 9 and take the first match as primary class; secondary classes may be recorded. Classes 1–3 never disappear (they can only be re-routed); classes 4–6 shrink with better rules and data; class 7 shrinks with proactive service but must always remain available; class 8 shrinks with reliability; class 9 should trend to zero.

**Mapping to authority scale.** Classes 1–2 are A4/A5 in the authority matrix (UNB-RCN-PLT-005); class 3 is an independence requirement on whoever decides; class 4 maps to DoA monetary limits (UNB-XIN-ERP-005).

Assignment is the selection of a person **within the eligible set**; it never confers authority (REQ-X-048; RR-REQ-X-048-r1). RR-REQ-X-048-r3 fixes precedence: eligibility (DoA for the action class, skill, sponsor scope, availability, conflicts, SoD history) is computed first; the mode chooses within it; an empty set falls through a declared chain ending in escalation.

Eliminated ≈ **38,950 h/yr ≈ 24.3 FTE** at H = 1,600 h [A] (economic-model.md:32), a 84% reduction. The residual is dominated by **ED and ER** (SPW-053/054): legally human, reducible only by routing (US intermediaries, reusable ED advice within its ~2-year currency) — not by automation.

**Cross-check against sourced cost pools [S] (industry/grt.md §8, which cites daf-landscape sponsor-cost-structure files):**
- Routine eligibility check for a listed domestic public charity ≈ **$0.14 per grant** (unbound:requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/industry/grt.md:206). At 800k grants [S baseline] that is ≈ **$112k/yr** [D] — consistent with the inventory's view that the routine lookup at a large national is already near-automated. **The conventional column above (≈6,667 h for per-grant lookup) represents a staff-checked process (community-foundation-like), where anchored labour is $180–323 per grant versus $7.9 at large nationals (grt.md:222).** The saving claimed by minimum-touch vetting is therefore large relative to conventional/community-foundation practice and small relative to large nationals.
- Non-standard diligence (ER, disqualified SOs, international ED) ≈ **$1.25M per 1M grants** (grt.md:207) → ≈ **$1.0M/yr** at 800k grants [D]. This is the pool that minimum-touch cannot automate; the grt.md implication (lines 224-229) is that savings come from routing exceptions to cheaper lawful paths, eliminating checks, dropping agreements and receipts on routine grants — **"automating routine verification further adds little."** This analysis agrees.
- Human approval ≈ $13 and manual exception ≈ $46 illustrative unit costs at $1/min (industry/svc.md:173-174) — consistent with 13 and 46 minutes per touch.
- Multi-sponsor reuse: with *s* sponsors sharing a recipient population with overlap *o*, the factual-verification portion scales as ≈ 1/(1 + o(s−1)) per sponsor [D formula], but the per-sponsor ED/ER, eligibility and reliance work does not shrink. Because the factual portion is already the cheap part, cross-sponsor reuse matters mainly for **ED reuse** — and that is the legally unverified part (SPF-ORG-008).

**Conclusion.** The 180-day automated design is sound as a *sponsor policy* with continuous event monitoring and dual-point checks; the big remaining cost is legal non-standard diligence, which is a routing and policy problem, not an automation problem.

**Why the 6–8 floor is not a floor.** It assumes a self-operated sponsor with in-house reconciliation and SoD roles held by fixed people (TVA-022; org §4). In S1, the independent reconciler, assurance, counsel and tax roles are external firms, platform roles are operator-side, and per-item SoD lets a cross-trained pool hold several SoD-separated duties. The genuine floor is **named authority holders per reserved decision class with coverage depth** — derived next — plus the board.

**When scale adds people and when it does not.**
- **Does not add people:** deterministic per-transaction work (approval of routine grants, eligibility checks with fresh evidence, acknowledgments, statements, postings, matching, fee computation) — zero marginal minutes; governance, executive, policy, BCP, tax filing, audit support — fixed per sponsor; platform roles — operator-side, step-wise.
- **Adds people linearly:** exception-driven authority roles — charitable compliance deciders (grants × e × m), gift acceptance (contributions × complex share × hours), service case owners (accounts × residual human-contact rate), treasury exceptions (payments × exception rate). At 100k accounts these are ≈82% of minimum-touch workload [D].
- **Adds people in steps:** partner/vendor management, security, engineering (S3), seasonal surge capacity.
- **Levers ranked (expected case):** exception share *e* and minutes *m* (each halving halves the compliance pool, economic-model.md:84-88); complex-gift hours (12 h baseline [A] vs ≈2 h minimum-touch [A] — the single most fragile assumption, SPF-ORG-006); December surge flattening by giving plans (TVA-030 unmeasured); proactive status for contacts.
- **Sensitivity check [D]:** if minimum-touch exception decisions keep the baseline e = 8% and m = 45 (e·m = 3.6 vs 0.9 assumed), SPW-060 alone rises from 7.5 to 30 FTE at 100k (÷1,600 h), and S1 staff from ≈41.3 to ≈69.4 FTE.

**Derivation of the minimum pool (payment chain, worst case item) [D].** The pair graph is bipartite, so 2 people satisfy all pairs except the three-distinct PA-2 rule (org §4:85). With per-item SoD evaluation against subject history (org §5.2:108), a cross-trained pool of *n* treasury-authorized holders can decide any item if ≥3 are available (or ≥2 under SPD-ORG-001). Coverage depth then sets the pool: **single-absence cover → n = 4; double-absence (year-end) → n = 5** (with the reconciler external). review-fin-ops B-2's ≈10+ counts six seats twice (unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/13-adversarial-reviews/raw/review-fin-ops.md:209) and over-counts because the same person may hold several seats on different items (SPF-ORG-003; SPR-ORG-001).

**Practical sponsor floor (S1) [D/A].** 4–5 named authority holders (executive, finance authority, compliance lead, operations lead, + 1 cross-trained), board, and external independent reconciler, internal audit/sampling, counsel and CPA. Not reducible further without SPD-ORG-002. Workload, not SoD, determines FTE above ≈10k accounts.

**What does NOT require distinct people.** Preparing and coordinating a case (cradle-to-grave owner) and deciding a *different* case; holding both treasury and compliance authority on different items; executive also serving as policy author (but then not publisher of that version); one person approving payee changes for some payees and releasing payments to others.

**Formulas.**
- Workload hours per role group *r*: W_r(A) = Σ_{i∈r} V_i(A) × m_i / 60, with V_i(A) = V_i(100k) × A/100k (linear drivers), V_i(100k) (fixed), V_i(100k) × (A/100k)^0.3 (step) [A].
- Workload FTE: F_r = W_r / (H × u); H = 1,600 h [A, economic-model.md:32], u = 0.80 [A, UNB-XIN-ECO-006 default].
- Authority floor persons: P_min = coverage-depth pool for the binding class (4 single / 5 double absence) [D]; floor FTE = P_min × s_min, s_min = 0.5 [A].
- Sponsor staff FTE = max(floor FTE, Σ_staff F_r); December peak heads = staff + Σ_{exception roles} F_r × (peak/avg − 1), peak/avg = 250k/(225+25k) = 2.5 at k = 3 [S, economic-model.md:61-67].
- Staff cost = FTE × C, C = $165k expected, $124.5k low, $250k high [A/S, economic-model.md:33].
- Exception-pool cost per account (economic-model form): 8·e·m/(60·H)·C [S formula, economic-model.md:45].
- Total people cost = staff cost + purchased services (counsel, IA/sampling, CPA, reconciliation review, PEO, fractional vCISO) [A].

Platform, custody, payment and AI inference costs are excluded (operator/vendor costs; AI inference immaterial below ≈$4 per dossier, economic-model.md:96).

- The '~$258/account' figure cited in the mission brief was not found; $272 is the sourced modelled figure.

**Status of every number in this report.** Economic targets ($258, $100, $50, $25, $10) are exploratory design targets, not facts. Model outputs are **theoretical outputs of an executed model driven by labelled assumptions**, not observations. Labels: [S] sourced, [A] assumption, [D] derived, [M] measured (report-18 benchmark only).

**Finding: no source states "$258".** A repository-wide search of unbound, daf-landscape (all branches), Echelon, EDF, Clarity and AI-Engineering found no "$258 per account" figure (only unrelated $258.x amounts in 990 extracts). The figure is reproduced exactly as the **arithmetic midpoint of the two illustrative estimates that the adversarial review cites**: ($243.84 + $272) / 2 = **$257.92 ≈ $258** [D]. Both are illustrations, not observations:

**Reference decomposition on a heterogeneous book (OM1, 100k accounts, modal inputs, executed):** sponsor operating cost ex-acquisition **$239**/account; incl. acquisition $299; incl. acquisition + custody (the 09-comparable scope) $307. Fund-borne cost (pool expense 26.3 bps [S] + custody) is a further **$457**/account — larger than the sponsor's own cost and invisible in the $244–272 figures. Under Monte Carlo uncertainty the same configuration is **P10/P50/P90 $289 / 388 / 570** — the modal $239 sits **below P10** because the sourced ranges are right-skewed (minutes per exception 30–**135**, exception share 2.8–**17%**, loaded cost to **$250k**; unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/15-economics/economic-model.md:29-33).

**Implication.** A $258 target is internally consistent only for a *self-operated, full-service* sponsor near 100k accounts at modal assumptions, and on the heterogeneous market book it falls **below the P10** of the propagated uncertainty (fewer than 10% of runs) rather than being a central estimate. It should not be used as a single design target (SPF-ECN-001, SPF-ECN-002; SPD-ECN-001).

Method: each target is tested against five operating models (OM) at five scales with the executed model (300 Monte Carlo runs per cell, seed 20261124). - **A sponsor** costs $5k–37k/yr to the platform plus ~$60k/yr of its own entity costs [A]; this is the cost that makes small sponsors uneconomic and that the tornado ranks first in platform models.
- **A service case** resolved by AI is ≤$0.50 (svc.md:172, illustrative); a human async case is ~$34 at modelled minutes. **A payment failure** is $5 automated vs ~$29 manual.

**Do minimum balances and fees reflect inherent cost or history?** On this model, **history and distribution, not inherent marginal cost.** The $100 (Fidelity, DED:66) and $250 (RCF, DED:65) minimum fees [S] are close to the *fully allocated* cost of a small account in a conventional/OM1 cost structure (OM1@100k small-recurring fully allocated $115) and above it under lean structures (OM3@1M $50; OM4 $28). **Other revenue forms.**
- **Manual processing fees** (check, wire, stop-payment, complex asset): acceptable only as disclosed, donor-affirmed, cost-based service charges with recovery ratio ≤1.10 (UNB-XIN-ECO-018, XID-ECO-002). The model shows check grants cost ~$4.50 vs $0.46 ACH; a fee that recovers that difference steers to ACH without profit. A fee that exceeds cost **creates an incentive to keep manual paths alive** — flag.
- **Platform fees / white-label**: same economics as institutional licensing; per-sponsor fixed component is needed because sponsor-level cost (~$37k platform + ~$60k entity per sponsor [A]) is the top tornado driver in platform models (SPD-ECN-003).
- **Bundled financial services** (investment management, model-portfolio sponsorship, sub-advisory 0–100 bps; DED:38-47): revenue that grows with retained assets and with product placement — **asset-retention and conflict incentive**; must be disclosed and separated from grant operations; profitability must never enter routing (UNB-XIN-ECO-012).
- **Float / interest on cash awaiting grant**: rewards slow grant payment — already rejected (XRJ-ECO-001).

**Models that encourage unnecessary work, asset retention or delayed grants:** per-grant transaction fees (delayed/withheld grants), asset-based fees and advisor/bundled fees (retention), above-cost manual processing fees (preserves manual work), float income (slow payment), outcome pricing per approved grant (unsafe approval; unbound:requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/11-OPERATING-ECONOMICS.md:14). The least-distorting combinations on this model are **(a) a declining asset fee with a transparent, disclosed cross-subsidy for a DigitalMinimal class, or (b) institutional licensing with separate per-sponsor and per-account components**; both still carry a retention incentive that can only be mitigated by disclosure and by payout-oriented product design, not eliminated.

**State variables.** Per run: sampled parameter vector *v*; segment activity multipliers *act_s* ~ lognormal(0, 0.15); per queue *q* ∈ {exceptions, complex, service, ops}: backlog *B_q(d)*, contractor FTE *C_q(d)*, pending activation day; account multiplier *α(d)*.

**Equations.**
1. Segment volumes (annual): grants *G_s = n_s·g_s·grants_mult·act_s*; exceptions *E_s = G_s·min(1, e·x_s)·(1−reuse)*; contributions *K_s = n_s·k_s·act_s*; complex *X_s = K_s·min(1, c_s·complex_share_mult)*; contacts *H_s = n_s·h_s·contacts_mult*; ACH returns *= K_s^simple·mix_s(ach)·r_ret*; reconciliation breaks *= (G_s + K_s − P_s + P_s/batch)·r_brk* (payroll items *P_s* reconciled per employer batch).
2. Base staffing per queue: *FTE_q = max(floor_q, ⌈A_q·h_q/(60·H)·headroom⌉)*, floors 1/1/1/2 (ops SoD); fixed roles reproduce the 09 step table (leadership 5/8/10, engineering 4+2·round(log10(A/1000)) ≤10, agent owners 4, security 1→3, intelligence 1→3, partnerships ⌈A/20k⌉ in self-operated models). Same structure as unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/15-economics/economic-model.md:23.
3. Daily arrivals: *λ_q(d) = A_q/(225+25k) · (k if d ≥ 225) · α(d) · Π arrival_mult(d) + one_off(d)*; Poisson draw (normal approximation above λ=30). *k* = December multiplier (unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/15-economics/economic-model.md:60-62).
4. Capacity: *cap_q(d) = (FTE_q + seasonal_q(d) + C_q(d)) · (H/250·60/h_q(d)) · Π capacity_mult(d)*, with *h_q(d) = h_q·Π handle_mult(d)*.
5. Backlog recursion: **B(d+1) = max(0, B(d) + a(d) − cap(d))** (unbound:requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/11-OPERATING-ECONOMICS.md:119), simulated 250 working days + 60 extension days to measure clearance.
6. Surge response: if wait *B/cap* > SLA and no contractors, contractors activate after `contractor_lead_days`; *C_q = min(0.5·FTE_q+1, ⌈B/(SLA·per_FTE_cap)⌉)*; released when *B ≤ 0.5·cap*. Seasonal staff = `seasonal_frac`·FTE in December (OM2–OM5: 0.5).
7. Measures: wait *W(d) = B(d)/cap(d)* (Little's-law days of backlog); SLA attainment = arrivals on days with *W ≤ SLA* ÷ arrivals; p90 wait = arrival-weighted 90th percentile of *W*; recovery = first day after window end with *W ≤ 1* in every queue (censored at 60); friction per 1,000 = (human contacts + exceptions waiting beyond SLA + 0.5·ops cases) ÷ account-years × 1000; exposure = Σ kind gross; uncontained = gross − contained; **control-effectiveness proxy** = contained ÷ gross ($-weighted).
8. Cost assembly: each line {usd, type, bearer, level}; staff = FTE × loaded cost; surge = (seasonal days × 1.3 + contractor days × 1.3) × loaded/250; AI = exceptions × $/dossier + accounts × interactions × $/interaction + grants × $/screen; insurance and legal scale by (1 + log10(A/1000)) as in the 09 cost lines; platform models add sponsors = ⌈A/accounts_per_sponsor⌉ × (platform service + onboarding/5) and sponsor entity costs.
9. Revenue: tiered/flat/subscription/transaction/employer/advisor/licensing/hybrid/cross-subsidy formulas in `revenue_per_account`.
10. Sensitivity: one-at-a-time low/high (tornado) at modal inputs; Spearman rank correlation of sampled inputs vs cost/acct across 300 runs.
11. Common random numbers: run *i* uses the same seed in every scenario, so scenario deltas are paired (`scenario_paired_delta_vs_normal`).

**Rank correlation of sampled inputs with cost/acct (Spearman ρ across 300 runs; joint variation):**

Tornado and rank correlation agree on the top group. AI inference and payment rails never enter the top 8; infrastructure enters only for the DigitalMinimal floor. Custody is not part of operating cost, so its ρ = +0.16 in OM4 marks the sampling-noise floor (≈ ±0.12–0.16 at n = 300): ranks below ~|0.2| are not distinguishable from noise (AI ×10 moved the 09 model by only 2.7%, daf-landscape@6b3083a:research/ai-native-daf-enterprise/09-financial-models/financial-and-staffing-models.md:104-112).

1. **Human minutes per exception × exception share (after determination reuse)** — top-3 in every full-service configuration (tornado swing 51% / 39% at OM1 100k). Unmeasured (TVA-002, TVA-003; GAP-001 per daf-landscape@6b3083a:research/ai-native-daf-enterprise/09-financial-models/financial-and-staffing-models.md:13). **Measure first**: shadow replay of a partner's grant history with timed reviews and recipient clustering for reuse.
2. **Loaded cost per FTE** — ρ ≈ +0.35 to +0.51 everywhere; the labour rate is unreconciled ($38.87–$86/h, TVC-020 via svc.md:161; unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/15-economics/economic-model.md:96 GAP-040).
3. **Complex-asset share × specialist hours** — top-3 for a market book with HNW/institutional segments (OM1 tornado ranks 2–3). Outsourcing to vendors moves cost to funds (fund-borne $350/gift [A]) — a bearer change, not elimination.
4. **Accounts per sponsor and sponsor-level cost** — the **#1 driver in every platform model** (tornado swing 105% at OM3 1M, 97% at OM4 1M). Not previously a parameter in the Unbound or 09 models. Sponsor fragmentation, not account count, sets the platform floor.
5. **December multiplier k and contractor lead time** — determine SLA attainment, not cost (k unproven, TVA-004).
6. **Grants per account** — linear on exception work; 6.2–13 observed range [S].
7. **Human contacts per account** — matters only for DigitalMinimal books (top-10 in OM4); immaterial for full-service books (consistent with daf-landscape@6b3083a:research/ai-native-daf-enterprise/09-financial-models/financial-and-staffing-models.md:110 5.5%).

**Do not matter much (within stated ranges):** AI inference price, infrastructure (except at the $10–25 floor where infra_per_account is top-4), payment rails, custody bps (fund-borne anyway), audit, data providers.

**Falsification tests.** The model's main conclusions flip if (a) measured exception-minutes-per-grant at a lean sponsor exceed ~12 (then $258 fails even for OM3 at 1M; executed bisection `targets.258.OM3_1M_max_exception_minutes_per_grant` = 12.4 min/grant) or are below ~2 (then $100 becomes reachable for full-service at 1M; bisection = 1.97); (b) real sponsors on a shared platform average ≥25k accounts (sponsor-level cost falls below $5/acct); (c) measured contact rates for small accounts exceed ~0.1/yr (DigitalMinimal $25 fails).

**Independence caveat.** Model, parameters and this interpretation were produced by one model family in one session; the replication of the 09 numbers checks arithmetic, not truth. None of this is independent validation (UNB-ECO-006).

WE-1 to WE-4 are deterministic (modal-input, noise-off) runs of the executed model; reproduce with `M.run_once(cfg, om, accounts, scenario, random.Random(0), noise=False)`.

**WE-1 Backlog arithmetic (OM3, 10,000 accounts, December peak k = 5).** Exception arrivals 2,870/yr; base rate = 2,870/(225+25·5) = 8.20/day; December = 41.0/day. Staffing ⌈annual minutes/(60·1,600)·1.15⌉ = 2 FTE + 50% seasonal; capacity per FTE/day = 6.4 h × 60 / 30 min = 12.8 → 38.4/day in December. Result: peak backlog 65, p90 wait 1.29 days, SLA attainment 100%. At 10k the 2-FTE floor gives slack; the same arithmetic at 100k (11 FTE, no floor slack) yields p90 wait 14.1 days (MC P50).

**WE-2 Simultaneous failures (OM3, 100,000 accounts).** k = 4, 25% staff absence days 225–239, vendor outage (0.02 unknown-state cases per account), service demand ×3, exception handle time ×2 during AI outage, ops arrivals ×5. Ops queue: 10,871 arrivals, peak backlog 6,507, SLA 28%, not cleared 60 days into the next year; service queue peak 6,989. Cost/acct $148.26 vs $147.00 normal; overall SLA 59%; gross exposure $65.5m of which $0.58m uncontained. Lesson: the 2-FTE ops floor with a 50%+1 contractor cap is the weakest point; ops needs a pre-contracted surge bench (SPD-ECN-004).

**WE-3 Incorrect AI outputs (OM3, 100,000 accounts).** Daily routine grant flow = annual grant dollars/250 = $16.62m; f = 1%, detection after 5 days ⇒ gross $0.831m paid in error (same form as unbound:research/daf-theoretical-enterprise-validation/15-economics/economic-model.md:106-108); recovery 60% [A] ⇒ uncontained $0.332m; potential §4966 excise on the taxable share 10% [A] × 20% [S] = $16,616. Post-payment review cases = grants/250 × 5 × 1% = 145. Operating cost unchanged; control proxy 0.871 vs 0.928. Detection time, not model price, is the lever.

**WE-4 DigitalMinimal unit economics (OM4, 1,000,000 accounts).** Accounts 15% inactive / 40% small recurring / 45% workplace. Modal cost $23.94/acct = account-level $11.82 + platform fixed $6.83 + sponsor-level $4.85 (+ identity). Staff 61 FTE ({'exceptions': 11, 'complex': 1, 'service': 10, 'ops': 9}); the ops queue (ACH returns on small-recurring debits plus reconciliation breaks, 15–20 min each at $1.719/min) is nearly as large as the exception queue, although contributions (16,515,000/yr) are mostly batched payroll items. Revenue: $9 (0.6% × $1.5k workplace) to $30 (small recurring $5k); employer $12 alone loses money. Viable only with ≥~$25/acct revenue or a disclosed cross-subsidy.

**WE-5 The $258 arithmetic.** ($508,000 × 12 / 25,000 + $27,200,000 / 100,000) / 2 = ($243.84 + $272.00) / 2 = $257.92 [D].

**Group cx — phases Seven (customer friction, DOM CXP), Eight (configuration, DOM CFG) and Nine (dashboards, DOM DSH).** The analysis is requirements-level only. No code was written or executed against Unbound. The data files were generated by Python scripts and every line was checked to parse. Referenced IDs were checked against an index built from the unbound reconciliation and discovery data files, including inventory.csv.

| Output | Records |
|---|---|
| interactions.jsonl (SPX) | 90 interaction steps across 7 personas |
| config-items.jsonl (SPG) | 120 configuration items, registers and policies |
| metrics.jsonl (SPM) | 84 candidate metrics across 14 audiences |

**Sources read:**
- Unbound baseline: ADM, AIN, UX, INT, UNB-UX, and the 19-questions specifications on operational intelligence, work queues, the shared dashboard framework, AI-discoverable contracts and sponsor configuration.
- Reconciliation: reports 10 and 13; UI requirements UNB-UI-*; gap requirements UNB-RCN-*; decisions RCD-*.
- Discovery: reports 11, 14 and 17; UNB-XIN-* requirements; findings.
- daf-landscape: `docs/sponsor-white-label-grant-policy-affirmations-v0.1.md` and `docs/daf-enterprise-ui-requirements-v0.1.md`, both at working-tree HEAD 14c954a.

**Evidence labels:**
- All effort seconds are **[A]** analyst assumptions: active customer effort per occurrence, not measured. No usability study, contact data or analytics exist for Unbound.
- Counts of interactions, configuration items and metrics are **[D]**, derived by counting the generated files.
- Thresholds marked [A] are illustrative.

**Limitations:**
- One model produced every judgement here. This is not independent validation.
- The legal characterisations (§170(f)(18), Reg E, Nacha, §4966/§4967) are taken from the requirement texts that cite them. Where noted, they are `unverified — general knowledge`; statute text was not re-read.
- The task cites "reconciliation report 13" for Forma/Folio. Report 13 is the architecture dependency analysis, which holds the Forma/Folio verification matrix. Report 10 holds the UI Forma/Folio gap analysis. Both were used.

Per persona. The step-level detail is in `interactions.jsonl`. Effort is the sum over one pass through each listed journey, in active seconds **[A]**. Effort for sponsor, administrator, employee and partner journeys is staff or organisational time, not end-customer time.

| Persona | Journeys | Steps | Eliminated | Changed (prefill, infer, default, derive, async, progressive, proactive) | Retained as is | Effort before [A] | Effort after [A] | Reduction [D] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| donor | 7 | 43 | 6 | 27 | 10 | 8,060 | 1,883 | 77% |
| financial advisor | 2 | 9 | 0 | 7 | 2 | 3,855 | 565 | 85% |
| charity | 1 | 9 | 3 | 2 | 4 | 9,900 | 1,920 | 81% |
| sponsor | 1 | 9 | 0 | 4 | 5 | 399,600 | 50,700 | 87% |
| administrator | 1 | 7 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 27,900 | 3,900 | 86% |
| employee | 1 | 6 | 1 | 3 | 2 | 13,200 | 6,180 | 53% |
| institutional partner | 1 | 7 | 1 | 3 | 3 | 21,000 | 7,980 | 62% |

Recommendation mix across all 90 steps [D]: retain 28, default 17, prefill 14, eliminate 14, proactive-notice 7, infer 5, progressive-disclosure 3, async 1, derive 1.

**Donor.**
- *Journeys:* open a fund, add money by ACH, give securities, recommend a grant, set up a recurring plan, add participants, ongoing servicing.
- *Removed:*
  - source-of-funds questionnaire (SPX-003; bank CDD rejected by XRJ-BNK-001);
  - micro-deposit round trip, replaced by instant validation, which UNB-XIN-PAY-002 already permits (SPX-011);
  - the standalone pledge question (SPX-026);
  - per-grant step-up for recommendations (SPX-027; XID-ADV-009);
  - annual affiliation re-attestation for most funds (SPX-037; XIF-ADV-018);
  - eligibility information requests that registry enrichment can answer (SPX-030).
- *Defaulted:*
  - funding allocation, purpose, recognition and communication preferences;
  - per-occurrence re-affirmation of recurring grants, replaced by a standing affirmation with event triggers (SPX-032; WL-13).
- *Highest-value change:* one grouped affirmation step on every grant (SPX-024; SPF-CXP-001).
- *Abandonment drivers [inference]:*
  - the document-and-selfie step (SPX-002);
  - the multi-day micro-deposit gap (SPX-011);
  - legal text density in affirmations;
  - re-entry when a session expires at review (UXA-4).
- *Repeat-contact drivers [inference, no contact data]:* the status questions "was my grant paid?", "where is my acknowledgment?" and "is my fund open?" (SPX-009, SPX-014, SPX-029, SPX-039). They become proactive catalog notices (SPF-CXP-003).
- *Phone-only donors:* the registered-device rule (UNB-XIN-SVC-004) blocks account-summary answers by phone (SPX-036). Keep the security goal but allow OTP to a verified channel for the account-summary class (XIF-ADV-018).

**Financial advisor.**
- *Journeys:* join a client fund; service many clients.
- *Removed or reduced:*
  - repeated identity proofing, by reusing firm-asserted identity where the firm contract carries assurance obligations (SPX-045);
  - firm-change re-entry, inferred from the HR/SCIM feed under UNB-XIN-CRM-007 (SPX-050);
  - manual per-client exports, replaced by a consented feed (SPX-052).
- *Retained:*
  - explicit role acceptance;
  - the clear client-context switch (wrong-client risk, TVC-011);
  - the acting human's own affirmation. AI never affirms.
- *Repeat-interaction driver:* co-advisor approvals for every grant. Use the any-one threshold under XID-ADV-004 (SPX-049).

**Charity.**
- *Removed:*
  - registration before the first grant (SPX-053; RR-UNB-GRANT-026-r1);
  - grantee receipt acknowledgment (SPX-056);
  - repeated vetting questionnaires per sponsor, since common evidence is reused as input under RCD-006 (SPX-061).
- *Retained:* destination enrolment and change controls (security) and supporting-organisation certification (law). Certifications are reused within their validity window.
- *Repeat-contact driver:* matching deposits to donors. Fix with structured remittance carrying the grant ID (REQ-X-077).

**Sponsor (officer).**
- *Dominant cost:* populating about 20 registers (SPX-064; XIF-ADV-004).
- *Change:* outcome questionnaire plus attestation of reviewed packs (Phase Eight).
- *Retained:* contract, board delegation, counsel approval of disclosure text, the A4 activation, and the opening-balance tie-out.

**Administrators.**
- *Eliminated:* manual impact assessment of policy changes, now simulated (SPX-072); human batch approval where the board has delegated routine approval to deterministic policy (SPX-075; RCD-005); cost thresholds, deferred (SPX-077).
- *Retained:* independent approval of policy changes.

**Employees.**
- *Eliminated:* the separate statement approval after close certification, pending RCD-038 (SPX-081).
- *Changed:* case summaries are machine-drafted and labelled under UNB-XIN-SVC-009 (SPX-082); attachments are extracted as Observations (SPX-083).
- *Retained:* sampled attestation (RCD-020) and verified-channel confirmation of assisted changes.

**Institutional partners.**
- *Changed:* default subscription sets (SPX-086); delivery calendars derived from provider profiles (SPX-087); migration mapping instead of donors re-entering data (SPX-088); default destinations with elect-out on partner exit (SPX-089).
- *Retained:* application registration, per-sponsor enablement and family-office consent.

**Totals [D from A]:** 483,515 s before and 73,128 s after across all listed steps. This sum is dominated by sponsor onboarding. It is not a customer-effort KPI. The KPI is defined in "Friction metrics".

**Not elimination.** No step was removed by moving its work to donors, advisors, charities or vendors. SPR-CXP-004 rejects one such idea.

These 28 steps stay. Most are made faster without removing the interaction itself, through prefill, passkeys, grouping or async completion. Basis classes are consent, legally required affirmation or document, donor control, and security step-up.

| ID | Persona | Step | Basis | How confirmed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPX-006 | donor | Program agreement and exclusive-legal-control acknowledgment | law (contract formation) and donor-control; sponsor control is the basis of the §170(f)(18) acknowledgment the sponsor later issues (UNB-RCN | Unticked checkbox; re-ask if agreement version superseded before submit |
| SPX-008 | donor | Review and submit application | law (application is an offer to contract) and donor-control | Review step meets UNB-UI-G-005; no second dialog |
| SPX-012 | donor | ACH debit authorization | law (Reg E §1005.10(b) for recurring consumer debits; Nacha authorization rules) — per UNB-XIN-PAY-001 | Authenticated explicit authorization; copy provided to donor |
| SPX-020 | donor | Amount (fixed or percentage) | donor-control | None |
| SPX-024 | donor | Sponsor required affirmations (benefit, pledge, purpose) | sponsor control evidence for §4967/§4966 compliance (UNB-RCN-GRT-010; WL-06/07); statute does not prescribe a donor statement — counsel conf | One grouped acknowledgment with one explicit action, statements visible verbatim, distinct |
| SPX-028 | donor | Review and submit | donor-control (A2+ action, UNB-UI-G-005) | Review step is the confirmation (no second dialog) |
| SPX-034 | donor | Successor designation | donor-control (succession policy, UNB-XIN-TRS-005) | Summary in words of the split |
| SPX-035 | donor | Change email, phone or authenticator | security (authenticator bindings are authority facts, XID-ADV-008; UNB-XIN-IAM-003) | Step-up plus notice to prior channel |
| SPX-036 | donor | Balance inquiry by phone | security; registered-device rule (UNB-XIN-SVC-004) blocks donors without the app (XIF-ADV-018) | OTP to verified channel acceptable for account-summary class |
| SPX-043 | donor | Request fund closure or transfer | donor-control and law (governed sponsor-to-sponsor transfer) | Consequence preview |
| SPX-044 | financial advisor | Accept invitation and role terms | consent and security | Unticked acknowledgment |
| SPX-047 | financial advisor | Switch client fund context | security (wrong-context risk, TVC-011) | Context indicator; drafts invalidated on switch |
| SPX-054 | charity | Enroll electronic payment destination | security (UNB-RCN-GRT-017; RR-REQ-X-005-r1) | Verified-channel confirmation |
| SPX-055 | charity | Change payment destination | security (UNB-RCN-WF-028; UNB-UI-S-060) | Confirm on verified channel; prior channel notified |
| SPX-058 | charity | Supporting-organization certification | law (§4966 taxable-distribution exposure for certain supporting organizations; UNB-RCN-REG-002) | Certification signed by charity officer |
| SPX-059 | charity | Decline a grant before release | charity control (RCD-045) | None |
| SPX-062 | sponsor | Contract and responsibility matrix | law (contract; REQ-X-064) | Signature |
| SPX-063 | sponsor | Board delegation resolution | law/governance (sponsor exclusive legal control; RCD-005) | Board resolution |
| SPX-068 | sponsor | Approve legal disclosures and affirmation text | law (sponsor counsel must approve; WL-05/22) | Counsel sign-off |
| SPX-069 | sponsor | Readiness checks and activation (A4) | law/governance (UNB-RCN-WF-009) | A4 sponsor-officer command; finance readiness by different principal |
| SPX-070 | sponsor | Opening balance tie-out | financial integrity | Approval |
| SPX-071 | administrator | Draft a policy change | sponsor control | Diff plus impact preview |
| SPX-073 | administrator | Independent approval of policy change | security/segregation (ADM-048) | Approver other than author |
| SPX-078 | employee | Stage assisted change for caller | security (UNB-RCN-ENT-016) | Customer confirms on verified channel |
| SPX-080 | employee | Sampled attestation of automated reconciliation passes | control (RCD-020) | Attestation |
| SPX-084 | institutional partner | Register third-party application | security (UNB-XIN-SAS-006) | Certification |
| SPX-085 | institutional partner | Per-sponsor enablement of certified app | security/sponsor control | Sponsor admin approval |
| SPX-090 | institutional partner | Family-office consolidated-reporting consent | consent (UNB-XIN-TRS-006) | Explicit consent |

**Rules that are never relaxed:**
- **Consent is never inferred** from silence, a pre-checked box, AI or unrelated activity (WL-06; UNB-RCN-GRT-010; SPR-CXP-001).
- **Separate consents stay separate:** a recurring-debit mandate is not a grant affirmation (WL-21). Affirmation evidence is per representation even when the UI groups the statements (SPF-CXP-001).
- **§170(f)(18).** The statutory element is the sponsor-issued acknowledgment stating the sponsor's exclusive legal control (UNB-RCN-FIN-001). It is retained and delivered proactively. The donor's acknowledgment of sponsor control at fund opening (SPX-006) is contract formation and donor understanding, so it is asked once per agreement version and never per contribution (SPF-CXP-007; counsel to confirm).
- **Legally required debit authorization** (Reg E/Nacha per UNB-XIN-PAY-001) is retained (SPX-012).
- **Donor control** is retained: amount, charity, successor shares, closure and transfer, reconsideration (SPX-020, SPX-034, SPX-040, SPX-043). These are the donor's advisory privileges. The sponsor retains legal control (IRC §4966(d)(2)).
- **Security step-up** is retained for authenticator, contact, payee and authority changes (XID-ADV-008, XID-ADV-009) and for workforce access. A passkey path must exist (WCAG 3.3.8; UNB-UI-A-005).

These definitions are proposed in RR-ADM-042-r2. They extend RR-ADM-042-r1, and all of them live in the single metric registry (RR-REQ-X-043-r1).

| Metric | Definition | Numerator / denominator | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer effort per journey | Active seconds on required interaction steps to complete a journey | Sum of instrumented step durations; median and p90 per journey | Needs step instrumentation. Reported as "insufficient coverage" when coverage is below 95% [A] |
| Abandonment by step | Share of journeys that enter a step and do not complete within 7 days | Journeys entering step s without completion in 7 days / journeys entering s | Points to the exact step, as ADM-047 asks |
| Repeat interaction rate | Completed journeys in which the same fact was requested more than once from the same principal | Journeys with a repeated ask / completed journeys | Uses the RR-AIN-007-r1 source log |
| Repeat-contact rate | Same principal and reason within 7 days (RR-ADM-042-r1) | — | Already defined |
| Resolution time | First contact or submission to outcome communicated | Distribution by case kind | A case closes only when the outcome is communicated (RR-REQ-X-048-r2) |
| Unnecessary data entry rate | Facts asked that were held or retrievable at the time | Asked-but-held-or-retrievable / asked | Uses the source log. Target trend is toward 0 |
| Contacts per 1,000 accounts by reason | RR-ADM-042-r1 | — | Status reasons are the main elimination target |
| Deflection | RR-ADM-042-r1, always shown with repeat contacts | — | Deflection without resolution is not success |

**Guardrails:**
- No individual staff ranking (SPR-DSH-003).
- Effort surveys are optional and always shown with their response rate.
- Telemetry carries no sensitive values (daf-landscape UI product rules).
- Each friction metric is paired with a safety counter-metric so that friction is never reduced by weakening a control: affirmation-evidence completeness (SPM-035) and the false-hold rate (SPM-033).

This section implements UNB-SMP-CFG-001. The sponsor answers questions about outcomes it can answer. Each answer derives configuration through a published rule, and everything else takes the pack default. The sponsor reviews one draft that shows the provenance of every value, then the draft goes through the normal policy lifecycle.

| # | Outcome question | Derives or selects (SPG) |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Who is the legal sponsor, and which bank and custody accounts will hold charitable money? | Legal sponsor identity and disclosure (contract record); fiscal year from public Form 990; FundsFlow draft; locale and time zone |
| Q2 | Operating model: does Unbound keep the books, or does an administrator or institution keep them? | BookOfRecord (release 1: Authoritative); FundsFlow; CapabilityEntitlement; OperatorAccessDelegation scope |
| Q3 | Who approves grants, up to what amounts, and has the board delegated routine approval to deterministic policy? | Delegation of authority and board delegations (retained); routing tier (REQ-X-017) |
| Q4 | Which donors do you serve: individuals, entities or trusts, advisor-referred? | Identity-regime applicability; legal-representative types; co-advisor mode default; affiliation attestation band (SPD-CXP-003) |
| Q5 | Which causes or organisation types will you not fund beyond what the law prohibits, and how should foreign causes be handled? | Sponsor grant restrictions (retained); additions to DiscretionaryGrantPolicy; InternationalRoute via intermediaries |
| Q6 | How will money come in: ACH, wire, check, public securities, complex assets? | RailObligation subset; validation method; acknowledgment timing; completed-gift rules; card and crypto items absent unless selected |
| Q7 | How will grants be paid, and who prints checks? | RailEligibility; DestinationEvidence; positive pay; unclaimed-property states (from payee states, not a sponsor choice) |
| Q8 | Do you offer investment options beyond a cash sweep, and is a counsel opinion on file? | Investment program menu and pool LegalBasis (retained); IncomeAttribution; buffer floor; AssetMeasure |
| Q9 | What are your fees, on what base and minimums, and who pays? | Fee schedules (retained); payer source; day-count from pack |
| Q10 | Self-service only, or dedicated managers above a balance? What are your service hours and holidays? | Servicing model; case calendars; routing policy |
| Q11 | What is your website, preferred terms (for example "grant" or "distribution") and languages? | Brand kit prefill; terminology aliases (protected terms locked); locales |
| Q12 | Do you want stricter controls than the reviewed defaults? (cooling-off, step-up, freshness, materiality) | Controlled overrides, tighten-only |
| Q13 | How often should donors receive statements, and how? | Statement cadence (SPD-CFG-002) |

**Result [D]:** 13 questions plus 14 explicit sponsor values, instead of 110 items surfaced at onboarding. The sponsor officer attests pack adoption (A4). Counsel reviews only deviations and the sponsor's own disclosure and affirmation text, which the law requires the sponsor's counsel to own (WL-05/22).

**Not delegated to AI:** AI may explain each question and prefill brand assets from the sponsor's public website (L2). It never answers the legal questions (Q3, Q5, Q8) for the sponsor.

section: Policy packs, explainable defaults, conflict detection, configuration simulation and controlled overrides
markdown:
Requirements-level design for UNB-SMP-CFG-002, RR-ADM-027-r1, RR-ADM-048-r1 and UNB-SMP-CFG-003.

**Policy packs.** The packs are PK-LEGAL-US-DAF, PK-RAIL-US, PK-ACCT-NFP, PK-ESCHEAT-US, PK-SERVICE, PK-SECURITY, PK-TIMING, PK-RETENTION-US and PK-OPS.
- Each item carries: reviewing authority and date, legal basis, default rationale, and an override direction (tightenOnly, lengthenOnly, sponsorChoice or none).
- Packs are semantically versioned and published under dual control.
- A sponsor adopts a pack by an A4 attestation recording the pack hash.
- Transactions and issued documents pin the pack version in force.
- Upgrade propagation is SPD-CFG-001; liability is SPD-CFG-003.

**Explainable defaults.** Every default is displayed as "From PK-x vN: <rationale> (basis: <citation>)". The same text is in the assistance contract (RR-REQ-X-051-r2), so the UI, help text and AI cannot diverge.

**Controlled overrides.**
- A deterministic comparator per value type checks the override direction. Days and business days are distinct types.
- Loosening is rejected unless a recorded counsel deviation exists, with an owner and expiry.
- Overrides are counted (SPM-057) and pack currency is monitored (SPM-058).

**Conflict detection.**
- Declared conflict rules in the Configuration Register are evaluated together with platform hard controls and pack baselines.
- Precedence follows REQ-X-018: stricter applicable law and platform safety prevail, and a sponsor may only tighten.
- An unresolved conflict blocks approval.

**Configuration simulation.**
- Before approval, the change is simulated against open items: grants, schedules, holds, payment instructions, fee accruals and pending statements.
- The last 90 days of decisions [A] are replayed under the proposed version, and changed outcomes are reported.
- A breach of a platform-safety parameter blocks approval (UNB-RCN-WF-021).
- Simulation runs in tenant scope on synthetic or tenant data and never posts.

**Configuration is a cost (UNB-SMP-CFG-003).** A new setting cannot merge without a register entry and an approved disposition. Platform-owned and eliminated items are absent from sponsor APIs and UI.

**Existing coverage:**
- REQ-X-051 (scope: APIs, inputs, configuration, workflow actions, dashboard widgets, email blocks and tokens).
- RR-REQ-X-051-r1: an AssistanceContract JSON Schema with required core fields, including validationRules, businessConstraints, permittedActorTypes, safe and prohibited actions, humanApprovalBoundary, outcomeExplanation and examples.
- UNB-RCN-ARC-001: one F# source generating OpenAPI 3.1, JSON Schema and the assistance contract, with a CI breaking-change check.
- The AI-DISCOVERABLE-CONTRACTS specification: AssistantCapabilityContract, FieldHelp and ActionHelp, assistance levels L0 to L3, caller-scoped discovery, and drift tests.
- RCD-025: AI help only on surfaces with a published contract.

**Gap (SPF-CFG-005).** r1 narrowed the kind enum and dropped dashboard widgets and email blocks. It also has no fields to explain why a default exists, which law or policy it comes from, which way it may be changed, or what changing it would affect.

**Required schema additions (RR-REQ-X-051-r2):**

| Applies to | Field | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| all | kind ∈ {apiOperation, configProperty, workflowAction, uiField, templateToken, **policyRule, policyPack, configItem, metricDefinition, dashboardWidget, reportDefinition, emailBlock**} | Restores the REQ-X-051 scope |
| config/policy | legalBasis {class: statute, regulation, guidance, contract, sponsorPolicy or convention; citation} | Purpose and constraint provenance |
| config/policy | reviewedBy {role, date}; packId@version; owner; changeFrequency | Accountability |
| config/policy | defaultValue; defaultRationale | Explainable defaults |
| config/policy | overrideDirection ∈ {tightenOnly, lengthenOnly, sponsorChoice, none} | Controlled overrides |
| config/policy | dependsOn[], affects[] (contract IDs); conflictRules[] | Dependencies |
| config/policy | consequenceModel {simulationEntryPoint, affectedObjectTypes[]} | Consequences, through simulation rather than prose |
| config/policy | disposition (from the Configuration Register) | Whether it is exposed at all |
| metric/widget | decisionSupported; decisionOwner; expectedAction; counterMetric; thresholds[{value, basisLabel S/A}]; knownLimitations; misleadingInterpretations | A metric explains its own purpose and risks |

**AI behaviour:**
- An explanation must cite the contract version and legalBasis. If legalBasis is missing, the AI says the basis is undocumented and does not infer one.
- A surface whose contract lacks a required field is not assistant-ready, and AI help is hidden there.
- AI may draft diffs (L2). It never publishes, never authors legal values, and never changes NBA ranking (UNB-SMP-DSH-001).

84 candidate metrics, 70 kept [D]. Every kept metric names the decision it supports, the expected action, an authoritative source, a freshness rule, limitations, misleading readings and incentive risks (`metrics.jsonl`).

**Design stance:**
- **Release 1:** role-composed views, not configurable dashboards (RCD-026). Tables and metric cards, with at most one accessible trend per view (UNB-UI-S-011), until Forma charts exist (DG-01).
- **Daily use:** staff work from the exception inbox and the NBA. Dashboards are for periodic decisions. Customer homes answer "what can I do, what needs me, what is in flight".

section: Drill-down, evidence, accessibility, exception queues, widgets, embedding
markdown:
**Drill-down.**
- Every tile drills to the population that produced it. For example, outcomes at risk → the exception inbox filtered by reason and age → the case workspace (UNB-UI-S-014) → the evidence and the source event.
- Drill-down never broadens scope. Filters are typed and permission-aware (shared dashboard framework).
- Cost figures drill to AttributedCost rows and then to the source events (UNB-XIN-ECO-022 AC-1).

**Evidence and provenance.**
- Every figure shows its as-of time and freshness (UNB-UI-G-003/F-006), its metric version, and either a snapshot id (official) or a watermark (live estimate).
- Official and estimated figures are labelled distinctly.
- No total is shown as reconciled while any component is stale (UNB-UI-S-011).
- Bitemporal "as reported" vs "as corrected" views are kept, and restated history is visibly marked.

**Accessibility.**
- WCAG 2.2 AA (UNB-UI-G-008/A-001).
- Every chart has a title, labelled axes, value labels, a text summary and a keyboard-reachable data table (UNB-UI-DS-018).
- Status is never shown by colour alone.
- Counter-metrics cannot be hidden on mobile (report 11).
- Mobile: donor, advisor and approval views are phone-complete; finance and close are desktop-first (RCD-026; UNB-UI-G-009).

**Exception queues.** The single exception inbox holds rule-created WorkItems only (RR-REQ-X-048-r2; UNB-UI-S-008). Dashboards link to it and never duplicate it as another queue. Routine items never appear (UNB-RCN-PLT-006).

**Widgets.** Widget definitions are versioned. Each declares a data contract, loading, empty, error, Unknown and stale states, and a safe drill-down (REQ-X-050). Widget assistance contracts follow RR-REQ-X-051-r2.

**Embedding.**
- Release 1 offers only a read-only grant-status card (UNB-UI-W-001), served from the sponsor's Unbound origin with a short-lived, sponsor-scoped token.
- Action embeds are excluded until the widget host exists (DG-03).
- Partner and sponsor embedding of dashboards is deferred.
- No third-party tracking.

Sources: reconciliation report 13 §2/§4 (dependency verification), report 10 §3/§4, `data/ui-component-gaps.csv`, and the 19-questions SHARED-DASHBOARD-FRAMEWORK-FORMA-FOLIO-CAPABILITY-ASSESSMENT. **These gaps are listed only. section: Single source of definitions for dashboards, exports and print
markdown:
This section implements RR-REQ-X-043-r1. It supersedes having three registries:
- the REQ-X-043 semantic layer;
- the UNB-XIN-ECO-007 economics registry;
- the REQ-X-049 work-queue metric contracts.

It also operationalises the parity requirements MON-023 and INT-016.

1. **One Metric Registry.** Economics and work-queue metrics are entries in it, not separate registries. Each entry carries the RR-REQ-X-043-r1 fields, plus decision, owner, expected action, counter-metric and suppression rule.
2. **Decision gate.** A metric without a decision supported cannot be registered. The 14 removed metrics are the precedent.
3. **Snapshot binding.** A figure is computed from one of:
   - a sealed FinancialSnapshot (UNB-XIN-EVA-003), for official and print figures;
   - a read model with a declared watermark, for live estimates.

   Every rendering, whether Forma tile, CSV, JSON or API export, or Folio print, carries metric id@version, snapshot id or watermark, scope and as-of time.
4. **Parity test.** For a given scope and snapshot, the dashboard, export and printed values must be identical. Statement publication is blocked on mismatch (SPS-DSH-001).
5. **Definitions travel with the figure.** Exports and prints embed the definition version and, for estimates, the label "Management estimate, not a financial statement" (report 11).
6. **No ad hoc computation in presentation layers.** Forma and Folio receive computed values and definitions. They never compute metrics, as the 19-questions architectural split requires.
7. **Change control.** A material definition change creates a new version, keeps the old one for comparison, and visibly marks restated history.

**Scope.** Mission phase Ten (competitive differentiation) and §18 (research-transfer candidates). Evidence base: `daf-landscape` (read-only; @054c1b8 cross-industry findings via `git show`, working-tree `research/` and `data/`) and Unbound reconciliation report 05 with `data/competitive-rollup.csv` (41 CAP rows, 755 evidence rows). **No vendor was tested, no contract was read, no logged-in portal was observed**; all competitor evidence is public-source, and all Unbound positions are *documented, not implemented* (requirements gate FAIL, `unbound:requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/10-EXECUTIVE-FINDINGS.md:8`). This analysis was produced by one model; any adversarial reading in it is a same-model perspective, not independent validation.

**Rows:** 114 comparison rows (`comparison.jsonl`, SPC-001..SPC-114) across 15 provider groups and 16 dimensions. Grades: V verified-documented, M marketing-claim, I reasonable-inference, U unknown. Assessments: P parity, D differentiation, DA defensible-advantage, ER easily-replicated, CS competitor-superior, NE needs-evidence.

**Conclusion:** no labelled evidence shows the model expands total DAF demand. The defensible reading is share redistribution in a growing market, with the CF segment best evidenced and the small-balance segment worst (tax headwind plus existing $0-minimum access).

section: Pass G: a well-funded competitor with the same technology
markdown:
Assume a competitor with ample capital builds the same architecture (journal-authoritative per-sponsor ledger, contract-first API, rules-first/AI-second routing, default packs, metering). Which Unbound advantages survive?

| Advantage | Type | Survives? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Journal-authoritative ledger, per-sponsor database, outbox | technology | No | Same technology by assumption; Unbound's own benchmark found the design holds at 5–10% of measured capacity [M] (`unbound:requirements/discovery/2026-11-23-cross-industry/10-EXECUTIVE-FINDINGS.md:83`), i.e. ordinary engineering, not proprietary |
| Contract-first public API, scoped OAuth, agent controls | technology/policy | No | Months of work; Chariot/Daffy already ahead |
| Measured SLOs, WCAG conformance, SOC transparency | practice | No | Cheap to copy; first-mover reputational value only |
| Discretionary-hold explainability, reconsideration | policy | No | A board policy any sponsor can adopt |
| Counsel/CPA-reviewed default packs | regulatory knowledge | No (delayed) | Purchasable legal and audit work |
| Full-history portability | policy | No | Copyable, and lowers Unbound's own switching costs by design |
| Not tied to AUM/affiliate revenue | cost-structure | Only vs incumbents | An unaffiliated entrant has the same freedom |
| Cross-sponsor data network | data | Only if Unbound reaches scale first | Today Ren, Foundant and Chariot have larger networks |
| Distribution contracts, operating track record, assured history | structural / switching cost | Would survive | **Unbound holds none of these today** |

**Verdict:** none of Unbound's *documented* advantages survives Pass G. What would survive — distribution contracts, a multi-year assured operating record (SOC 2 Type II periods, clean audits), executed migrations, and network scale on the charity and sponsor sides — must be earned through execution. Strategy should therefore prioritise speed to measured, assured operation in one segment over breadth of designed capability. Caveat: this pass is a same-model adversarial perspective, not independent validation.

**Evidence labels.** [S] sourced, [A] assumption, [D] derived by stated arithmetic, [M] measured (report 18 only). Derived figures in this report were computed by executing arithmetic in Python during this session; no benchmark, test or simulation was run. Economic targets ($258/$100/$50/$25/$10) are exploratory design targets, not facts.

**Independence.** All analysis, including the thirteen stakeholder passes, is one model applying documented methods. It is not independent validation. Clarity's own held-out research found the current method no more accurate than an unstructured answer, with assumption exposure as its one clear strength (clarity-framework@200a9eb:research/2026-framework-improvement/README.md:19-21); EDF's performance claims are unestablished (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/README.md:17-35).

**Headline conclusions.**
1. R3 (architecture) is the best-evidenced recommendation; measured headroom rules out brokers, workflow engines and distributed services for release 1. The open risk moved from throughput to availability and recovery of fail-closed components, especially the platform hold registry, which the benchmark did not place in a separate database.
2. R2 is not falsifiable as written: $258 appears in no source (it is the midpoint of $244-$272 [D]) and $10 fully allocated sits below documented single components ($14.40 custody; $9 low-case exception labour [S]); at 100k accounts $10 funds 6.1-8.0 loaded FTE and nothing else [D].
3. R8 has no reference point: five different floors exist for different scopes, and the 6-8 figure is cited to a record (TVC-018) that does not contain it. A roster-derived floor must precede any target.
4. Minimum-touch (R1, R4) has hidden fixed costs: the detective sampling that makes auto-approval auditable (~1,521 reviews/month for +/-0.5 pp at a 1% error rate [D]) and a fallback that must be hold-and-notify because human review cannot absorb December volume.
5. R7 is a legitimate progressive-commitment step only if provisional status is machine-enforced; the observed correction rate on verified items means several of the 41 positions should be expected to change.

**What Clarity is, in its own words.** "A working framework for making beliefs, assumptions, evidence, confidence, ownership, monitoring, and reassessment explicit" with three core questions: *What do I know? What is currently justified? What would make me reconsider?* (clarity-framework@200a9eb:README.md:3-9). It states it is **not primarily a decision framework** (clarity-framework@200a9eb:README.md:13-20) and that it **does not perform diagnosis** -- EDF does (clarity-framework@200a9eb:README.md:41-55; clarity-framework@200a9eb:docs/framework-interactions.md:36-48).

| Posture (claim stage) | Discovery, commitment or reassessment | clarity-framework@200a9eb:docs/assessor-guide.md:47-49 | -- |

**Gaps in the method that affect this application (stated, not repaired).**
- Confidence Debt is "Core" but has **no definition anywhere in the repository**; Burden Externalization, Governance Debt and Resolution Debt have only one-line notes (clarity-framework@200a9eb:research/2026-framework-improvement/baseline/current-limitations.md:131). Where this evaluation uses them, the working reading is stated inline and is the evaluator's interpretation: *Confidence Debt* = confidence carried forward above what evidence supports; *Assumption Drift* = "an assumption gradually becomes treated as fact" (clarity-framework@200a9eb:docs/framework-evolution/apollo-challenger-reassessment.md:177-179); *Trigger Drift* = "a signal gradually stops producing reassessment" (same file, 171); *Burden Externalization* = work or risk moved onto parties outside the decision; *Governance Debt* = controls or reviews that are required but not resourced.
- **Clarity's own evidence boundary.** On a held-out 50-case benchmark, current Clarity was "no more accurate than the same model with no method", "much less useful" (2.2 vs 3.9 of 4) and longer; "its one clear strength is making assumptions explicit" (clarity-framework@200a9eb:research/2026-framework-improvement/README.md:19-21). Its gains were reproduced by a plain three-sentence instruction (clarity-framework@200a9eb:research/2026-framework-improvement/README.md:37). **Consequence for this report:** the Clarity results below are reasoning maps whose main value is assumption exposure; they are not evidence that any recommendation is right.

(echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/README.md:13-15) while Clarity says it is not primarily a decision framework. Preserved, not resolved. **What EDF is, in its own words.** "A systems understanding framework with a diagnostic grammar ... used to explain how a system produced an outcome and to identify the highest-leverage opportunities for influencing future outcomes"; "not primarily a decision framework" (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/specification.md:11-17). Specification v0.3, status *working draft* (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/specification.md:1-5).

**Diagnostic grammar (required sequence, echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/specification.md:39-54):** 1 System Context (Primary System, Context, Focus) -> 2 Outcome (factual, not interpretive) -> 3 Manifestation(s) (observable signals) -> 4 Origin Network (technical, human, organizational, environmental, financial, regulatory; "rather than a single root cause") -> 5 Propagation (physical, informational, organizational, financial, human) -> 6 Evaluate Evidence ("Separate direct observation from inference") -> 7 Control Points ("may differ from origins") -> 8 Rank Control Points (influence, controllability, cost, confidence; "does not need false precision") -> 9 Diagnostic Sufficiency ("Do we understand enough to take the next responsible action?").

**Required output elements (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/specification.md:150-168):** System Context, Primary System, Context, Focus, Outcome, Manifestation(s), Origin Network, Propagation, Evidence, Control Points, Control Point Ranking, Confidence, Diagnostic Sufficiency, Unknowns, Next Responsible Action. Template: echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/templates/edf-2-complex.md.

**Levels (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/complexity-levels.md:9-15, escalation triggers echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/complexity-levels.md:101-115):** EDF-0 rapid, EDF-1 standard (several plausible origins), EDF-2 complex (multiple interacting systems, disputed origins, higher consequence). "Consequences are high or action is irreversible -> increase depth regardless of label." All eight recommendations here meet at least one EDF-2 trigger except R5 (EDF-1).

**Evidence boundary (respected throughout).**
- "Coherent enough to use as a working diagnostic grammar. Its performance claims are much less mature." Not established: cross-executor reproducibility, causal improvement from System Context, better control points than alternatives, evidence-sensitive updating, superiority to natural analysis or neutral structure, validated quantitative confidence (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/README.md:17-35).
- Registry state (2026-09-22): HY-EDF-004 (better control points) *suggestive*; HY-EDF-005 (independent executors agree) *unsupported*; HY-EDF-008 (value beyond neutral structure) *unsupported*; HY-EDF-007 (Origin Network vs Propagation distinct) *suggestive* (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:research/registries/hypothesis-registry.json).
- Confidence labels are qualitative, not probabilities: Low, Low-Medium, Medium, Medium-High, High (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/framework-engineering/claim-and-confidence-policy.md:61-71).
- Control-point dimensions "are heuristics, not a validated scoring system ... no fixed weights" (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/framework-engineering/claim-and-confidence-policy.md:123-127); "leverage" is a heuristic judgment (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/model.md:131-133).
- Diagnostic Sufficiency "is action-relative. It is not a certificate that the diagnosis is true or complete" (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/README.md:95); "Higher-consequence or irreversible actions require stronger evidence" (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/framework-engineering/claim-and-confidence-policy.md:115-121).
- Independence: "Named analytical lenses produced by one model ... are not independent replications" (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/framework-engineering/claim-and-confidence-policy.md:91-97); Diagnostic Calibration was **not** used because it requires materially independent analyses (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/diagnostic-calibration.md:15-21).

**Adaptation declared.** EDF diagnoses how an outcome was produced. The eight items are prospective recommendations. Each EDF record therefore diagnoses the **observed condition the recommendation responds to** (the Outcome field states only documented facts), and records the recommendation's own predicted outcome separately as `prospective_outcome_hypothesis`, which is outside EDF's diagnostic scope. Each record also carries a `claim_state` for the recommendation's core claim using the claim-policy vocabulary (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/framework-engineering/claim-and-confidence-policy.md:47-59); that policy governs EDF research claims, so applying its states to Unbound claims is the evaluator's adaptation. Prior use: the landscape transaction-economics package used EDF fields informally ("These are **hypotheses**, not observed universal causes", daf-landscape:research/transaction-economics-evidence-package-001-2026-11-11.md:82-87); Echelon's `edf-diagnostic-packet` "does not perform an EDF diagnosis" (Echelon-AI-Native-Enterprise-Design-Framework@763ff8c:case-studies/daf/generated/analysis.md:309-311).

Each record follows the EDF v0.3 required output elements (echelon-diagnostic-framework@710d54c:docs/edf/specification.md:150-168). Confidence labels are qualitative. Control-point rankings are heuristic orderings. `claim_state` and `prospective_outcome_hypothesis` are declared adaptations (see method section).
